topic: For finite-population two-stage randomized saturation experiments, fix saturation-label count K, cluster-size bound b, rational treated-count table, and a rational direct/saturation contrast over bounded own-treatment-by-saturation potential outcomes. Allow arbitrary joint laws over saturation labels and feasible treated subsets and arbitrary measurable estimators. Prove endpoint completeness by an explicit multilinear extension, derive a polynomial-size rational convex primal/dual orbit game for fixed K,b with implementable optimal correlated design and nonlinear estimator, and extract rational epsilon-saddle certificates including all zero-probability faces. Prove uniform conditional subset randomization is without loss, give the finite primal-dual feasibility characterization of when optimized common-probability independent saturation is minimax, and prove a strict correlated-saturation advantage for the certified two-size-three-cluster instance and its infinite rational contrast neighborhood. Preserve the actual exact-count observation hypergraph rather than replacing it by a pairwise conflict graph, and do not claim an elementary closed-form equality classification, growing-cluster separation, or exact rational optimizers. The applied consumer is Baird--Bohren--McIntosh--Ozler's randomized-saturation design and its direct/spillover analysis. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Bernoulli lifting plus Jensen gives endpoint completeness for every fixed observation hypergraph; perspective-coordinate minimax duality and response/assignment/observation histograms give the orbit game; a rational 78-decision procedure and 17-orbit prior certify 1.3649753<R*<=1.364981422, while a 15-orbit prior proves R_ind>1.3659 for c=(3,-1,-1,-1), with the gap persisting for nearby rational contrasts. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Complete the polynomial Turing bit-complexity proof for orbit-kernel construction, conic weak optimization, rational epsilon-certificate extraction, and continuous-estimator decoding, including all zero-mass faces. EARLY KILL TEST: Independently reconstruct the orbit kernel for cluster sizes (3,3,4), compare selected response-histogram likelihoods and every assignment-orbit normalization with labeled enumeration, and rerun the saved rational certificate verifier; any mismatch stops K2 or the strict-comparison claim until resolved. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_boundedcluster_endpoint_orbit_minimax.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the unrestricted finite-population minimax design-and-estimation problem for a rational direct/saturation contrast under exact-count two-stage randomization reduce exactly to an endpoint game indexed by response, assignment, and observation-hypergraph orbits?

source_refs.claim: Randomized saturation designs identify direct and spillover contrasts through two-stage randomization, but their optimal-design analysis uses a regression model and conventional estimators.
source_refs.author: Sarah Baird, J. Aislinn Bohren, Craig McIntosh, and Berk Özler

source_refs.claim: For a no-interference binary-outcome ATE, unrestricted designs and estimators reduce to a low-dimensional minimax problem with a nonlinear minimax estimator.
source_refs.author: Timothy Sudijono, Edgar Dobriban, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.excerpt: The exact robust Gaussian minimax-regret design and a terminating all-minimizer receipt are open.
Replace the pairwise-variance surrogate with a terminating certificate for the exact robust all-selector game.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature and prior runs meet at the same proof boundary. The closest unrestricted minimax work collapses no-interference binary potential outcomes to a few aggregate counts, whereas exact-count saturation reveals different own-treatment-by-saturation coordinates through a coupled observation hypergraph. Existing saturation papers optimize power or variance for specified regressions or inverse-probability estimators, and the banked exact-hit run proves only a sharp covariance image and a pairwise-variance surrogate without a converse for the full all-estimator value. The missing step is a lossless endpoint reduction for the hypergraph likelihood, followed by a perspective formulation that remains closed when assignment probabilities vanish.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An equality theorem would map the original worst-case squared-error problem over bounded potential-outcome arrays and all measurable estimators to a finite convex primal/dual endpoint-orbit game and decode a saddle point into an implementable correlated design and nonlinear estimator on every probability face.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the closest application-facing motivation and formulates the direct/spillover design tradeoff in the language used by saturation experiments.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interference makes outcomes depend on cluster treatment intensity -> two-stage saturation randomization exposes direct and spillover contrasts -> conventional power calculations optimize restricted estimators -> seek exact worst-case optimal design and estimation over bounded schedules

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the finite-population decision-theoretic reduction and posterior-mean nonlinear minimax estimator proof, replacing the no-interference count state by exact exposure-response histograms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It allows both unrestricted assignment mechanisms and unrestricted nonlinear estimators for bounded finite-population potential outcomes, matching the desired equality except for interference.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the assignment-design/exposure-mapping factorization and joint exposure-probability bookkeeping to define the exact observation kernel before optimizing the estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its exposure mapping is the standard interface between an interference design and the potential-outcome coordinates actually observed.

open_problems.open_problem: For fixed saturation-label count K and cluster-size bound b, can the exact-count observation-hypergraph orbit game be constructed and weakly optimized in polynomial Turing time with rational ε-saddle certificates and total estimator decoding on zero-probability faces?

source_refs.claim: Minimax precision under structured outcomes leads to mixed-strategy optimal experimental designs, with implementability and randomization-inference constraints treated as genuine design restrictions.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

source_refs.excerpt: The exact continuous-action squared-loss game is a finite convex quadratically constrained program.
Each exact program certifies one population size.
Exact enumeration uses 2^K domination inequalities, |J| coefficients, and assignment truth tables.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Abstract minimax and group-averaging arguments establish neither a Turing-polynomial construction nor an auditable certificate. Labeled assignments and response tables are exponential, orbit multiplicities can carry large encodings, and perspective coordinates become singular when an assignment or observation has zero mass. The banked multi-arm result stops at a continuous-action convex QCQP for one population size, while the binary truth-bound result explicitly retains exponential truth tables. The first changed proof step is to replace labeled enumeration by canonical response/assignment/observation histograms and prove exact stabilizer-weighted likelihood normalization without collapsing the observation hypergraph to pairwise conflicts.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A polynomial Turing bit-complexity theorem would bound orbit enumeration and rational kernel construction, supply separation oracles and conic weak optimization, extract outward-rounded rational ε-saddles, and decode each certificate into an implementable measurable estimator with a valid risk bound on every zero-mass face.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames mixed randomization as an optimization object and separates statistical optimality from implementability constraints, which is the right lead-in to certified algorithms.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Structured potential outcomes induce a minimax design problem -> optimality may require a mixed assignment law -> implementability turns existence into a computational question -> seek a bit-certified polynomial algorithm for the exact saturation game

method_exemplars.technique: Use permutation-group averaging to justify orbit restriction, then replace existential symmetrization by stabilizer-weighted rational kernel construction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its minimax proof exploits assignment symmetries; the desired result must make the analogous quotient explicit, exact, and polynomial.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the finite decision-problem representation of unrestricted nonlinear estimation, retaining perspective variables so an estimator is recovered from a rational saddle solution.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest unrestricted design-estimator game, while exact-count interference introduces precisely the orbit-enumeration and zero-face difficulties.

open_problems.open_problem: What finite primal-dual condition is necessary and sufficient for a common-probability independent first-stage saturation law to be minimax, and can correlated saturation labels be certified as strictly better on an explicit rational instance and an open rational contrast neighborhood?

source_refs.claim: Under interference, designs between cluster and stratified extremes can improve bias or variance, but the analysis optimizes conventional estimators under a structured outcome model.
source_refs.author: Chencheng Cai, Jean Pouget-Abadie, and Edoardo M. Airoldi

source_refs.claim: Without interference, independent treatment assignment remains minimax over bounded finite-population outcomes even when arbitrary nonlinear estimators are allowed.
source_refs.author: Peter Hull

source_refs.excerpt: primal activity, an LP dual certificate for each active lambda, and stationarity form a finite certificate.
identify conditions under which the robust allocation coincides with a conventional power-optimal saturation allocation.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The no-interference bounded-outcome rectangle tensorizes across units and supports independent assignment, while an exact-count saturation observation hypergraph couples which response coordinates are jointly revealed. Existing saturation-design work studies moments of the saturation vector for fixed estimator classes, and the banked KKT theorem optimizes a simplex image rather than deviations in the full polytope of correlated label laws. Enlarging that feasible set changes both extreme points and tangent cones. The first missing step is to represent independent common-probability designs as a constrained image inside the correlated assignment-orbit polytope and test every correlated tangent direction using full-game dual slack; strict slack and continuity must then turn a numerical separation into a rational neighborhood theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite rational primal-dual feasibility system would be equivalent to independent-saturation minimaxity and would yield either a rational correlated-design/least-favorable-prior certificate with a strictly smaller risk on a stated small cluster instance and explicit rational contrast neighborhood, or a certificate ruling out separation.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative directly compares saturation-design families and shows that interference changes which saturation dispersion is desirable.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Saturation dispersion governs bias and variance -> interference makes standard extremes nonuniformly attractive -> existing optimization fixes a conventional estimator and structured model -> ask when cross-cluster correlation itself lowers unrestricted worst-case risk

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the bounded-outcome minimax proof of independent Bernoulli optimality, isolating the tensorization identity that fails under saturation interference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the sharp independence benchmark for the same finite-population decision loss once interference is removed.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over invariant-design group averaging, then use normal-cone and complementary-slackness arguments to compare the independent image with the full symmetric design polytope.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired characterization compares two invariant assignment classes, making finite-sample minimax symmetrization the closest proof template.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its randomization-based direct/spillover estimators and conservative variance theory as the conventional inference benchmark for the decoded nonlinear minimax estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the established estimation rung for the same two-stage saturation design even though it does not optimize correlated label laws.

open_problems.open_problem: Is conditional uniform randomization over feasible treated subsets minimax without loss when first-stage saturation labels and second-stage treated subsets may have an arbitrary joint law across clusters?

source_refs.excerpt: Hence Z_c conditional on {Z_c in S_k} is uniform on S_k.
The equality persists after deleting L_c conditional on every realized target assignment.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The exact-hit factorization proves conditional uniformity only because independent Bernoulli assignment gives equal probability to every subset with the same treated count; it does not justify replacing an arbitrary joint design by that conditional law. Under unrestricted bounded schedules, a nonuniform subset law changes which response coordinates are revealed, and cross-cluster dependence changes joint observation likelihoods. The missing first step is a finite-group minimax symmetrization that averages the design, transports every potential-outcome schedule, and maps every measurable randomized estimator back without increasing worst-case risk while preserving the entire exact-count observation hypergraph and the contrast.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite Hunt–Stein-style invariance theorem would prove equality of minimax values before and after imposing conditional uniformity within every size-specific exact-count slice, with explicit symmetrization maps for joint designs, bounded schedules, and arbitrary measurable randomized estimators.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly motivates the two randomization stages and makes within-cluster assignment symmetry part of the design-based setup.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Two-stage experiments randomize cluster saturation and then units -> standard analyses use symmetric within-cluster assignment -> arbitrary joint mechanisms make that symmetry nonautomatic -> prove a minimax invariance principle for conditional uniformity

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt design-based minimax symmetrization using the within-size unit-permutation group and an equivariant estimator kernel.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a decision-theoretic route from permutation invariance to minimax randomized design, exactly the missing justification for conditional subset uniformity.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt orbit sufficiency and posterior-mean estimator construction while retaining the exact observation-hypergraph labels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its unrestricted-estimator orbit reduction is the nearest template for proving that symmetrization preserves the full minimax value.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the exact-hit minimax construction be extended from equal cluster size to every bounded heterogeneous size profile while preserving exact assignment-orbit normalizations and both cluster- and person-weighted direct/saturation contrasts?

source_refs.excerpt: The results concern fixed n, fixed K, equal cluster sizes, distinct interior rational saturations.
Extend the exact-slice target to heterogeneous cluster sizes using the floor-ceiling deployment mixture.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Both exact-hit runs use common cluster size as a load-bearing restriction: there is one exact-count slice cardinality, one hit matrix, and one response-type alphabet. The reviewer-proposed floor-ceiling deployment does not by itself preserve person-weighted contrasts or likelihood normalization under an arbitrary correlated design. The first changed proof step is to replace the single response type by a size-tagged histogram and prove that every orbit multiplicity reproduces labeled enumeration for every treated-count slice; only then can the estimand map distinguish equal-cluster and equal-person weights before minimax duality.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For every fixed K and size bound b, a size-tagged finite orbit-game equality would give exact rational normalization, explicit estimand vectors for cluster- and person-weighted contrasts, and an implementable optimal correlated design and nonlinear estimator for every heterogeneous cluster-size profile.

writing_exemplar.why: Its practical two-stage formulation makes unequal cluster sizes and estimand weighting choices part of the causal question rather than a secondary correction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Two-stage interference experiments naturally have unequal clusters -> exact-count exposure probabilities and welfare weights then differ by size -> equal-size minimax formulas do not transport mechanically -> build a size-tagged orbit game that preserves both design and causal weighting

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over size- and mechanism-aware randomization inference for vectors of direct and spillover contrasts, replacing linear estimators by the orbit-game minimax rule.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest two-stage design-based framework in which assignment mechanisms and vector contrasts are explicit.

method_exemplars.technique: Use exposure-probability normalization to verify each size-tagged likelihood and each cluster- versus person-weighted estimand map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem must preserve the exact mapping from assignments to observed exposure coordinates across unequal clusters.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the endpoint-and-orbit minimax reduction extend from anonymous own-treatment-by-saturation outcomes to known exposure mappings whose exact assignment observation hypergraphs have bounded automorphism-orbit complexity?

source_refs.claim: Known general interference can be encoded by an exposure mapping, with estimators and variance calculations determined by exposure probabilities under the assignment design.
source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow and Cyrus Samii

source_refs.claim: Without meaningful restrictions on interference, design-based causal inference can be impossible or fail to concentrate even under structural models.
source_refs.author: Guillaume W. Basse and Edoardo M. Airoldi

source_refs.claim: Under spatially decaying interference, cluster-randomized design and Horvitz-Thompson estimation can be jointly tuned for near-optimal rates and asymptotic normality.
source_refs.author: Michael P. Leung

open_problems.why_unsolved: Anonymous saturation exposure is unusually symmetric: unit labels within equal-size clusters collapse to response histograms. A general known exposure mapping preserves only automorphisms of its assignment-to-exposure hypergraph, and bounded cluster size alone need not yield polynomially many response or observation orbits. Aronow and Samii provide the exposure interface but retain inverse-probability estimators; Basse and Airoldi show why an assumption-free arbitrary-interference extension cannot succeed; Leung obtains rates only after spatial decay and estimator restrictions. The first proof step that changes is the response-histogram sufficiency lemma, which must become an automorphism-orbit sufficiency theorem with a sharp complexity boundary or fail by counterexample.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give verifiable orbit-complexity conditions on an exposure mapping under which unrestricted bounded-outcome minimax risk equals a polynomial-size convex orbit game with a decoded design-estimator pair, together with a counterexample family showing exponential blow-up or loss of identification when those conditions fail.

writing_exemplar.why: Its design-exposure-estimand decomposition is the natural language for motivating a destination beyond anonymous saturation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interference makes treatment vectors too detailed -> exposure mappings encode substantively meaningful conditions -> inverse-probability methods use induced exposure probabilities -> ask when exposure-map symmetry also compresses the full minimax design-estimator problem

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over exact exposure-probability kernels and joint-exposure variance bookkeeping, replacing inverse-probability weights by an estimator selected in the finite minimax game.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems are governed by the same assignment-to-observed-exposure kernel.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the design-based impossibility construction to prove the negative side when automorphism compression or exposure support is insufficient.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the relevant proof boundary showing that no assumption-free extension to arbitrary interference can work.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt joint design-estimator lower-bound comparisons and dependency-controlled limit theory to benchmark orbit-game solutions under structured non-anonymous interference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It jointly analyzes experimental design and causal estimation under a nontrivial interference restriction beyond partial interference.

literature_map:
1. Hudgens and Halloran (2008, JASA, doi:10.1198/016214508000000292) established direct, indirect, total, and overall effects under two-stage randomization and partial interference.
2. Baird, Bohren, McIntosh, and Özler (2018, REStat, doi:10.1162/rest_a_00716) made randomized saturation an econometric design problem, optimizing power through a clustered regression model.
3. Liu and Hudgens (2014, JASA) supplied large-sample randomization inference for two-stage partial-interference experiments.
4. Rigdon and Hudgens (2015, Statistics & Probability Letters, doi:10.1016/j.spl.2015.06.011) obtained exact binary-outcome intervals by permutation inversion, exposing the missing-potential-outcome obstacle.
5. Aronow and Samii (2017, AOAS, doi:10.1214/16-AOAS1005) formalized the design/exposure-mapping/estimand interface and exposure-probability Horvitz-Thompson inference.
6. Basse and Airoldi (2018, Sociological Methodology, doi:10.1177/0081175018782569) proved that unrestricted interference can destroy design-based identification or concentration.
7. Kallus (2018, JRSSB, doi:10.1111/rssb.12240) and Kallus (2021, JRSSB, doi:10.1111/rssb.12412) framed experimental design as minimax mixed-strategy optimization under structural restrictions.
8. Bai (2023, Journal of Econometrics, doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.10.009) used permutation invariance to establish finite-sample minimax randomization in a no-interference setting.
9. Jiang, Imai, and Malani (2023, Biometrics, arXiv:2011.07677) developed unbiased estimators, conservative variances, tests, and power formulas for direct and spillover effects in two-stage designs.
10. Cai, Pouget-Abadie, and Airoldi (2022, arXiv:2203.09682) showed that interference changes optimal saturation dispersion, but optimized conventional estimators under a linear interference model.
11. Leung (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2111.04219) obtained near-optimal cluster designs and asymptotic normality under spatially decaying interference.
12. Yu, Ma, and Liu (2025, arXiv:2501.14602) studied minimax designs with spillover and carryover using Horvitz-Thompson estimation and conservative variance analysis.
13. Liu, Shaikh, and Zhong (2026, arXiv:2607.04257) separated finite-sample-valid sharp or bounded-null tests from asymptotically valid weak average-spillover tests.
14. Hull (2026, arXiv:2608.09812) and Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, arXiv:2608.13822) broadened bounded no-interference minimax analysis to independent assignment and nonlinear estimation.
15. The live tension is that saturation papers permit interference but restrict outcome models or estimators, while unrestricted bounded-outcome minimax papers omit exact-count observation hypergraphs, correlated saturation laws, and rational computational certificates.
